claims.body: The Blues are the league’s best for chance quality, but the Golden Knights are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. Our lean: the Blues’ chance quality wins out.

claims.head: Expect a grind
claims.call: The game’s pace score is below 95, slower than either team’s usual.
claims.see: Fewer than 63 shots between them at 5-on-5, on goal or wide, which usually means 53 or fewer shots on goal on the scoreboard.
claims.body: The Golden Knights play some of the league’s slowest games, and so do the Blues. We think this one is even quieter than either team’s usual.

claims.head: The Golden Knights’ power play outclasses the Blues’
claims.body: On the power play, Vegas is one of the league’s best, but St. Louis is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Every penalty the Blues take could cost them.

notes.text: Logan Mailloux is out long term and has not played this season. He is a top-four defenseman. Adam Jiříček has taken his spot beside Philip Broberg.
Dylan Peterson was added to the roster on Oct 11 and has played beside Ross Johnston and Pius Suter.

STL.head: The Blues have a hill to climb
STL.body: Even though St. Louis has home-ice advantage, Vegas has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Blues can pull it off if they get good looks.

VGK.head: The Golden Knights should have the upper hand
VGK.body: Even though St. Louis has home-ice advantage, Vegas has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Blues’ way back in is getting good looks.

story.head: The matchup inside the matchup
paras: The Blues are 3-3-1. The Golden Knights have won two in a row, the last a 6-2 rout of Calgary.
It’s strength against strength: the Blues are the league’s best for chance quality, but the Golden Knights are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey.
